Subject: Draft: Dedicated runtime fairness & SLA runbook

Team / Talya —

Attaching a first pass at a customer-facing runbook for Dedicated capacity SLA behavior, focused on the questions Orchid raised in last week's call (queueing behavior during bursts, reserved headroom, and fallback guarantees). This is intentionally operational: it explains what we'll commit to in contracts vs. what the runtime will do automatically.

High-level goals:
- Make explicit how we handle reserved GPUs vs. best-effort bursts
- Define admission control and preemption behaviors that map to SLA language
- Provide measurable signals (metrics) the customer can cite in escalations

Two quick asks from our side:
1) Marissa / Sales: can you confirm which contractual tier Orchid will be in (reserved 48-GPU pool, monthly) so we can align numbers?
2) Karthik / Infra: please sanity-check the technical remedies and the metrics list — I added a sample metrics export as an example.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_sla_runbook_v0.3.pdf (draft), sample_queueing_metrics_2026-07.csv

Thanks Diego — useful start. A couple of commercial points I want clarified before we share this with procurement: 

- The runbook distinguishes between "guaranteed throughput" and "best-effort bursting". Can we map those to explicit contractual units? For Orchid that means: baseline preserved for 48 reserved GPUs, and up to 25% bursting for up to 10 minutes per hour. I need those numbers reflected exactly if we will put them in SOW language.
- Also, please add an explicit section that outlines customer responsibilities (e.g., pushing concurrency caps, not spiking without notice) so we can use it in the mutual action plan.

If Karthik confirms the runtime behavior we can send this to Talya and Procurement as "engineering-runbook for contract" and loop in Legal for the fallback text.

Diego / Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for sending this. A few points from Orchid's side:

1) We need a clear, auditable definition of "fallback" when we exceed reserved throughput. Specifically: when requests are routed to compatible model variants (lower precision/quantized) or cross-region fallback occurs, what is the allowed latency delta and how is quality measured? We cannot accept a vague "may fallback" clause.

2) Regarding queueing: our product team is worried about tail latency during synthetic traffic spikes. We want guarantees for p99.9 token generation latency under the reserved pool (not bursting). If you cannot guarantee a hard p99.9 bound, we need a documented mitigation plan (e.g., headroom reserve, pre-warm pools) and a runbook step that Orchid can trigger to request temporary carveouts.

3) Auditability: we will run quarterly checks. Please include which metrics Redwood will provide (and retention): per-route token latency histograms, queue_depth, preemption_events_count, and a signed daily availability report for the reserved pool.

We appreciate the example metrics file — can you confirm the latency buckets and the retention window?

Talya Singh
VP, Platform Engineering
Orchid Financial

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Talya Singh <talya@orchidfin.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Dedicated runtime fairness & SLA runbook

Great questions. Technical notes to align the runbook with what the runtime can actually promise: 

- Hard SLA bounds for p99.9 token latency are very brittle at the model level (quantization, sequence lengths). We can commit to an operational SLO: p99.9 <= 450ms for baseline reserved workload under the following constraints (these must be in the SOW):
  * requests conform to the agreed prompt length distribution (avg tokens/request <= 128)
  * per-tenant concurrency limit set to 24 active streams by default
  * aggregated pool CPU/GPU utilization < 85% (we provide headroom metrics)

- Fallback behavior: we will define three fallback tiers in the runbook — model-variant fallback (quantized compatible variant), degraded-throughput mode (short-lived queue admission), and cross-region failover. For each tier we will state expected median latency and max additional token latency (e.g., model-variant: median + ~60ms/token; cross-region: median + ~200-400ms depending on region). Provide those as guidance, not contractual guarantees except where explicitly called out.

- Admission control & fairness: we operate a weighted fair-queueing scheme per-customer with admission thresholds. Customers with reserved capacity will get strict admission priority until their baseline quota is exhausted; bursting is admitted only if headroom is available (we track headroom in a rolling 5m window). Preemptions are last-resort and will only drop best-effort jobs (we log preemption_events_count).

- Metrics: we can produce per-route histograms (1ms buckets up to 1s, then aggregated tails), queue_depth (sampled 1s), preemption_events_count, headroom_percent. Default retention is 90 days; extended retention can be added as a paid add-on.

I've attached a sample CSV from a controlled test showing how those histograms look. I also added a short appendix to the draft runbook with the admission-control thresholds and the names of the runtime signals we will expose.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — good progress. Summary and next steps: 

1) Marissa: please confirm Orchid's requested numeric carveouts (you suggested baseline + 25% burst for 10m/hr). If they confirm, we'll include those numbers in Section 2 (Contractual Guarantees).
2) Karthik: please convert the operational SLO language into two blocks in the runbook: (a) Contractual guarantees (the metrics we commit to measure and report daily/quarterly) and (b) Runtime behavior descriptions (what we will do automatically — model fallback, admission-control thresholds, and preemption rules).
3) Talya / Procurement: we'll route a revised runbook and a short appendix that maps each runtime action to the expected customer-visible impact (latency delta / throughput delta). Once we get confirmation on carveouts, I'll loop Legal to draft precise fallback clauses.

I'll circulate v0.4 after Karthik's updates. If Orchid wants an on-call window during a spike, we can schedule a 2-hour mitigation drill with infra engineers.

Diego
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
